assertions.source: at every level l the WZW/WRT monodromy trace ∈ [−2,2] (elliptic) — it is UNITARY (positive-definite Gilmer–Masbaum form; det-1 unitary ⇒ eigenvalues on the unit circle ⇒ tr=2Re(λ)∈[−2,2]). including l=8 (A₅ keystone, tr≈1.0). It CANNOT carry the hyperbolic τ_binding=2.6424>2. scope-(b) exclusion, cited invariant WRT unitarity — the fibre(root-of-unity)/observable(real-q) archimedean-continuation wall.

result.verdict: CLASSIFICATION (ii) structural analogy needing a bridge — NOT a derivation. The Hitchin/WZW monodromy (Laszlo–Pauly–Sorger) supplies exactly the right OBJECT TYPE for τ=tr B (SL₂ det-1 bar-even WZW/Hecke trace, Prop 5.1 = [2]²−[2]) and confirms the keystone's A₅ as the finite level-8 SU(2) monodromy image (Prop 5.3). But it does NOT bridge to τ_binding=2.6424: (a) the specific element σ₁⁻¹σ₂ at real q0 = 2.033 ≠ 2.6424 (distinct [2]_q-rationals); (b) at every root of unity the monodromy is UNITARY ⇒ elliptic |tr|≤2 (l=8 A₅ gives 1.0), so no literal WZW element carries the hyperbolic τ>2 (cited invariant: WRT unitarity). This is the SAME archimedean-continuation wall the corpus already names (fibre root-of-unity unitary vs observable real-q hyperbolic; keystone §Frontier bwS0_eq_hecke). The Hitchin paper makes the wall vivid (A₅ = level-8 finite monodromy; binding τ = its hyperbolic continuation) but leaves the owner-gated keystone continuation as the sole route. Not passed off as a closure. No fit; no c_k wired.
